newsitem.title: USA: Physician Support plunges after warning.
newsitem.headline: Physician Support plunges after warning.

text.p: Shares of Physician Support Systems Inc on Friday lost more than half their value after the company issued a warning on its fourth-quarter earnings.
Physician Support, which provides business management services to hospital and physicians, was down 9-1/16 at 7-1/2 in early afternoon trading on the Nasdaq.
Still, some analysts said the company's long-term outlook was strong.
"At this price, the company is a terrific buy," said David Francis, an analyst at Punk, Ziegel & Knoell.

Physician Support's performance has been hampered by an extended restructuring at its Spring Anesthesia Group unit. But Francis expects the company to show improvement in the second half of 1997, once the Spring turnaround is completed.

Francis said other health-care information providers have been hard hit lately after issuing profit warnings. In time, the fundamentals of the business should pull most stocks out of the doldrums, he said.
"But investors have to be selective in this sector," Francis said.

Physician Support late Thursday said it expected to break even in the fourth-quarter before merger and restructuring costs. Analysts on average had expected the company to earn $0.15 a share, according to a First Call survey.
The company sees fourth-quarter revenues of about $21 million and $74 million for the year ended December 31.
"While we are disappointed by these short-term results, we believe that solutions are in place that will lead to improved profitability in 1997," said Peter Gilson, Physician Support's president.
The company said unexpected seasonal factors also contributed to the fourth-quarter weakness.

Separately, the company said Thursday it acquired PhyServ Solutions Inc, based in Jackson, Michigan, for an undisclosed price. The management of PhyServ is being put in charge of Spring and will help the troubled unit move towards profitability, the company said.

"While it will take some time for PhyServ management to fully implement their systems and operating methodology at Spring, we believe that the PhyServ management team will provide a consistent and profitable approach to anesthesiology billing nationwide," Gilson said.
